head: Starbucks came to Korea
with a partner.
slides.sub: And Korea became one of its biggest markets.

image.label: A coffee cup on a Seoul street at dusk
image.brief: 해 질 녘 서울 골목 위 커피 컵 하나. 실제 로고는 쓰지 않음.

head: 1999: a first
store in Seoul.
body: Starbucks Coffee Korea opened its first store near Ewha Womans University in July 1999.
It was a joint venture, owned half by Starbucks and half by Shinsegae, a Korean retail group.

image.label: A café opening near a university gate
image.brief: 대학교 정문 근처에 새로 연 카페 앞 학생들. 1999년 분위기.

head: Why not
go alone?
body: Starbucks knew coffee and its brand. Shinsegae knew Korean property, landlords, hiring and shoppers.
Prime corners in Seoul are hard to win without local relationships.

image.label: Two hands joining puzzle pieces
image.brief: 두 손이 퍼즐 조각을 맞추는 장면.

head: Entering a new country.
How do you go in?
body: You have a strong brand and a proven store model, but no local network.

options.text: Franchise to many local operators for speed
options.feedback: Fast, but harder to keep every store consistent. Keep swiping.

options.text: Go alone and learn the market yourself
options.feedback: Full control, but slower learning. Keep swiping.

options.text: Form one joint venture with a strong local retailer
options.feedback: This is what Starbucks did in Korea. Keep swiping.

image.label: A map of Korea with location pins

head: No franchises.
Every store run directly.
body: The joint venture ran its stores itself instead of franchising them. That kept service and design consistent as it spread across the country.

image.label: Baristas in matching aprons behind a counter
image.brief: 같은 앞치마를 입은 바리스타들이 카운터 뒤에서 일하는 장면.

head: Korea's phones
came first.
body: In 2014, Starbucks Korea launched Siren Order, letting customers order ahead on their phones. It was reportedly the first service of its kind in the Starbucks world.

image.label: A phone showing an order-ahead screen
image.brief: 휴대폰 화면 속 미리 주문 화면. 실제 앱 화면은 쓰지 않음.

slides.label: Starbucks stores in Korea by 2021
body: Korea grew into one of Starbucks' largest markets by store count.

image.label: A night map of Korea dotted with lights
image.brief: 불빛이 촘촘히 박힌 한국 야경 지도.

head: 2021: Starbucks
sells its stake.
body: Starbucks sold its 50% share. Shinsegae's E-mart and Singapore's sovereign fund GIC bought it, and the stores kept the Starbucks name under license.

image.label: A signed contract on a boardroom table

head: Each side brought what
the other lacked.
body: A partnership works when both sides gain something they can't build quickly alone, and both win when the business grows.
Starbucks brought the brand and model. Shinsegae brought local know-how. Running stores directly kept the brand consistent while the partner adapted it to Korea.

head: Borrow what you
can't learn fast.
body: Entering a new market? Decide what you must control and what you would be smarter to borrow.
**Try it today:** list what your next market requires. Which of those could a partner give you faster than you could build it?

image.label: A coffee cup steaming on a window ledge
image.brief: 창가에서 김이 오르는 커피 한 잔.

가맹점 없이 전 매장 직영이라는 점은 회사 자료 기준입니다.
사이렌 오더(2014년)가 스타벅스 전 세계 최초 모바일 주문 서비스라는 설명은 회사 발표 기준이라 "reportedly"를 붙였습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2014년 사이렌 오더 '세계 최초'는 이번 검색에서 미확인.
2021년 매장 수 1,500곳 이상(연말 약 1,600곳으로 보도)과 스타벅스 시장 중 순위는 회사 자료와 보도로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2020년 12월 1,503~1,508개 확인. '2021년 1,500개 이상'과 일치.
2021년 스타벅스 본사 지분 50% 매각(이마트 17.5%, GIC 32.5% 인수, 이마트 지분 67.5%)과 라이선스 유지는 당시 발표와 보도 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2021년 7월 이마트 17.5% 추가(총 67.5%), GIC 32.5% 인수 확인.
